title: Choose the visual world for The Boss Remembers
question: The roll assigned Court Deck. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Court Deck
options.lineage: French-suited playing cards on a baize card table
options.thesis: Every build is a hand of cards; the boss's adaptation is the card it plays from the hand it drew.
options.viewport: Felt top bar with run and record; You and The Boss as face-up court cards with HP, ATK, DEF, DEX pips; Prepare / Fight / Aftermath tabs; the Armory as a grid of item cards, three loadout slots outlined on the felt; Begin round anchored bottom right.
options.risk: Tips into casino kitsch if felt and gold spread into the shell; the baize must stay a ground, never ornament.

raised.raise: Numbers rank by scale alone: HP and damage set large, every other figure small, no boxes to signal importance.
All saturated colour lives inside card faces; the shell stays baize, white stock and ink.
Layout snaps to a card-width module; columns are whole card widths.
Suit pips stand for STR, DEF, DEX and HP on every screen, read at a glance, with text kept for the first read and screen readers.
One card form at three sizes (full in the Armory, mini in the log, pip in the Versus bar), never a second component.

options.label: The Fencing Manual
options.thesis: The duel recorded as numbered plays in a fight book, with the boss's notes in the margin.
options.viewport: Fighters as paired line figures at the top of a ruled page; plays numbered down the page; the boss's reasoning as margin notes beside the play it answers.
options.risk: Familiar: parchment and ink is where most medieval game UIs land, and close to the look being replaced.

options.label: Duel Score
options.thesis: The fight as a bilateral score: you left, the boss right of a centre staff, each attack a block whose height is its damage.
materials: solid, hatched and dotted symbol blocks
options.viewport: A vertical centre staff with both fighters' columns; time rises upward; prep and boss panels flank the score.
options.case: Fuses strongly for the fight replay (two sides, time, damage as length); weaker for the shop and preparation screens.
options.risk: Abstract notation can feel clinical rather than tense.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Stats as axes that morph the fighters' type live.
options.viewport: A giant glyph per fighter that thickens with STR.
options.case: Loses both axes: players don't identify with type specimens, and it hides the duel.
options.risk: Becomes a type demo instead of a game.

options.label: Lexicon Plate
options.thesis: Fights as entries, colour only inside bordered plates.
options.viewport: Dense text column with a shoulder index of rounds.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as a dictionary, not a duel.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The duel built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Grid-built HP numerals over a neutral grotesk UI.
options.case: Loses both axes: cold, no duel tension.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every round a numbered catalog entry in coded colour.
options.viewport: Pulse plot of HP lines on black.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels hide game state.
options.kept: State speaks in a consistent code.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: Pixel HP numerals over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro-novelty, unrelated to a medieval duel.
options.kept: One form repeated at many sizes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A browser RPG companion screen: dark panels, gold accent, stat bars, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Two character panels with bars, tabbed prep below, primary gold button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from countless game dashboards by design.
